grammar.title: Infinitive Constructions: 'Hay que', 'Tener que', 'Ir a'
grammar.explanation:
Spanish has several common constructions that use infinitive verbs (the base form ending in -ar, -er, -ir):

• Hay que + infinitive: One must / You have to (impersonal)
  Hay que hervir el agua. - You have to boil the water.

• Tener que + infinitive: To have to (personal)
  Tengo que cocinar la cena. - I have to cook dinner.

• Ir a + infinitive: Going to (near future)
  Voy a freír el pescado. - I'm going to fry the fish.

These constructions are extremely common in everyday speech and are essential for giving instructions in recipes.
